newsitem.title: UK: Aerodata sticks with Scott Pickford.
newsitem.headline: Aerodata sticks with Scott Pickford.

text.p: Australia's Aerodata Holdings Ltd said on Friday it would proceed with its plan to buy a stake in British geoscience and engineering services group Scott Pickford Plc, despite a statement from Scott Pickford earlier today that it had received a bid approach for the whole group.

"Aerodata...considers its position to be unchanged and it intends to proceed...with the share exchange announced on December 13, 1996 and with any offer it may make, or be required to make, for all of the issued shares it does not own in Scott Pickford," the company said in a statement.
Under its original plan, Aerodata had intended to buy 2.5 million of SP's shares at 48 pence each to give it a 20 percent stake in the British company's curent capital.
Scott Pickford would then be offered Aerodata shares giving it 4.3 percent of its share capital, and the intention had been to pursue joint marketing thereafter, but remain separate firms.

Although it gave no details of the possible offer approach, Scott Pickford said earlier that an undisclosed company (which it dubbed "a substantial and credible party") had said it would likely make an offer for the whole firm at about 53p per share -- 5.0 pence more than Aerodata's buy.

"Aerodata believes that the size, strengths and synergies of itself and Scott Pickford will enable management and staff of Scott Pickford a larger degree of autonomy and input into the merging of both parties activities," the Australian firm added in its statement.
During the morning Scott Pickford's share price was marked up, though no volume was recorded. By 1000 GMT the share price was indicated at 49 pence, up 4-1/2 pence from Thursday's close.
